channel.title: Acme: Tech News
channel.description: Articles about software, publishing and the open web.

item.title: Publishers and protocol builders gather around an open-web agenda
item.description: Protocols for Publishers brings independent newsrooms and protocol builders together in Toronto to discuss direct reader relationships, media provenance and systems that are harder for dominant platforms to capture. The agenda treats open protocols as practical publishing infrastructure, not an abstract ideal.

item.title: New data maps which podcast hosts shows are leaving and joining
item.description: Podnews is tracking changes in podcast RSS domains to show where programs are moving. Its latest 30-day sample found 2,182 host changes among 547,788 recently checked podcasts, with an interactive table showing gains and losses for each service—an unusually concrete view of the open podcast market.

item.title: A practical guide to following blogs with RSS and OPML
item.description: Feeder explains how blogs on WordPress, Substack and Medium expose RSS feeds, and how OPML import moves an entire subscription list into one reader. It is a useful current primer on reading independent sites without creating an account for every platform.

item.title: ActivityPub draft sharpens the decentralized social web
item.description: A fresh W3C editor’s draft lays out ActivityPub’s two interoperable layers: server-to-server federation and a client-to-server API for creating, updating and deleting content. The split matters because sites can adopt either layer, then add the other to join a broader ecosystem of portable clients and decentralized publishing tools.

item.title: Firefox 157 refreshes its interface and restores Compact Mode
item.description: Mozilla’s Firefox 157 rolls out a redesign across desktop and mobile with rounded tabs, updated icons, themes and a smaller Compact Mode restored after user requests. The release is a notable investment in an independent browser engine—and a reminder that user feedback can still reverse a product decision.

item.title: Apple’s unified EU app terms take effect
item.description: Apple’s new EU terms permit notarized apps through alternative marketplaces or the web and allow outside payment offers, while replacing several fees with commissions that vary by distribution and payment method. Independent developers gain more routes to users, though lawyers say questions remain about compliance with the Digital Markets Act.

item.title: California creates a major employment credit for local news
item.description: California’s new Community NEWS Act ties refundable tax credits directly to newsroom employment: $20,000 for each of the first five journalists, $15,000 for additional staff, plus credits for part-time workers and new hires. The program could direct about $40 million a year to local outlets, though critics warn wealthy chains may also benefit.

item.title: Judge dismisses publishers’ search-summary lawsuits
item.description: A federal judge dismissed antitrust suits from Chegg and Penske Media over Google summaries that reuse publisher material while reducing site visits. The judge said publishers had only an expectation—not an agreement—that indexing would bring traffic, while acknowledging the economic harm to online creators may be a matter for legislators.

item.title: European software-freedom report puts interoperability first
item.description: Free Software Foundation Europe’s annual report argues that interoperability rules must work in practice, giving independent developers and free-software projects access to platform features controlled by dominant vendors. Its review also covers device neutrality, public-code campaigns, legal education and the group’s 25th anniversary.

item.title: Reddit sets November date to shut down RSS feeds
item.description: Reddit says its RSS feeds will stop Nov. 13 and its public API will close in March 2027, citing scraping and abusive traffic. Moderators get a Devvit relay option, but outside feed-reader users get no replacement. The decision turns a major body of public conversation into licensed platform data and removes another open-web access point.

item.title: Social media’s democratic reputation declines worldwide
item.description: Pew finds 64% of Americans believe social media has harmed democracy, while negative assessments have risen in 16 of 26 countries surveyed in both 2022 and 2026. The Netherlands now records the bleakest view at 70%. The international shift suggests the platform-governance debate is no longer chiefly an American argument.

item.title: Voting-machine suspicions spread across federal agencies
item.description: A Reuters investigation reconstructs how a probe of Puerto Rico voting machines expanded across federal agencies before the midterms. Officials found no evidence that hackers altered votes, but the inquiry widened anyway. Interviews with more than two dozen people show how unsupported suspicions became a government-wide effort with consequences for election trust.

item.title: W3C pilots direct support for open-source web projects
item.description: The World Wide Web Consortium has begun a pilot program to support open-source projects that implement web standards. The effort is meant to strengthen collaboration around web technology, speed adoption and improve interoperability—exactly the connective tissue the open web needs but rarely funds well.

item.title: Eclipse launches vendor-neutral software sovereignty initiative
item.description: The Eclipse Foundation has formed a vendor-neutral initiative to help organizations map technology dependencies, evaluate open-source alternatives and make more deliberate infrastructure choices. The practical goal is reduced lock-in and greater control over critical software stacks.

item.title: World News Day essay calls for journalism to rebuild trust together
item.description: Daily Maverick co-founder Branko Brkic argues that news organizations must stop treating one another as the main competition, acknowledge how monopoly-era habits alienated communities and cooperate against disinformation and platform power. His prescription joins media criticism to a concrete democratic mission.
